# Adversarial review — mAb TDM v0.41.0

**Reviewer:** Buffy (Freebuff)
**Date:** 2026-09-29
**Scope:** UI/information design, statistical correctness, pharmacometric correctness.
**Method:** full read of `src/model.js`, `src/bayes.js`, `src/chart.js`, `src/ui.js`, `index.html`; the built artifact
(`complementtdm.html`, v0.41.0) driven live in a browser at 1280 px and 390 px; the engine re-driven directly
through `ECU.bayes.runFit` / `intervalScan` / `reportHtml` to produce every number quoted below.
**Changes made to the app:** none. (`complementtdm.html` was regenerated by `node build.mjs` so it could be
opened in the browser; it is a generated artifact and no source file was modified.)

Every figure below is reproducible from the snippets given. Findings I could not reproduce are in §D — read that
before spending time on anything.

---

## 0. Verdict in one paragraph

The engine is in better shape than a 4,000-line browser PK app has any right to be. The likelihood, the censoring
method, the Laplace/MCMC plumbing and the model transcriptions held up under adversarial probing, and I found **no
wrong-PK bug**. What I did find is that the app is *excellent at computing and careless about deciding what to
compute and what to say*. The three numbers a clinician acts on — the half-life, the credible interval, and the
attainment probability — are each defensible in isolation and misleading in combination: the half-life is a
one-compartment number in a two-compartment model and is 3.5× short; the interval excludes the app's own assay
error, which changes the headline probability by up to 19 points; and the attainment probability is coloured
green on a latent quantity while the printed report prints `P 100% (100–100%)`, a degenerate interval that
asserts certainty the model does not have. The chart is organised around peak concentration when every clinical
question is about troughs, and the phone layout — which v0.17.0 specifically rebuilt — clips its own legend and
offers no way to read a value off the screen. And v0.41.0's new "treated before the first dose?" gate, added to
stop a wrong-number failure mode, made the single most common TDM consultation unanswerable.

## 2. Statistics and inference

### A1 — The band and the probability exclude the app's own assay error *(High)*

`simulateDraws` returns the **latent** concentration per posterior draw. The residual term
`SIGMA.ADD + SIGMA.PROP·pred²` is applied only inside `makeOfv` (the likelihood), never to the predictive
distribution that produces the band, the trough quantiles or `probAbove`. So `P(trough > target)` is
P(**true** concentration > target), not P(the number the lab will report > target).

This is disclosed — [ui.js:1215](src/ui.js#L1215) says *"credible interval for the true concentration (it does not
include assay error, so a future measured value may fall outside it)"*. So it is not a hidden error. It is a
**design** failure: the quantity a TDM consult turns on is *"when the next sample is drawn, is the reported
number above target?"*, and the app never computes it.

Standard eculizumab patient (70 kg, PNH, 900 mg q14d ×8, troughs 78/95/82/88, target 75). Reconstructing the
predictive interval with the app's own `SIGMA` (`ADD` 19.1, `PROP` 0.0185):

| Day | App median | App band [5–95] | App P | Predictive band if Σ counted | P if Σ counted |
|----:|-----------:|-----------------:|------:|-----------------------------:|---------------:|
| 42  | 78.4 | 70–87 | 73% | 58–99 | **61%** |
| 56  | 87.6 | 78–99 | 100% | 64–111 | **81%** |
| 70  | 93.2 | 83–107 | 100% | 68–118 | **88%** |
| 112 (next dose) | 100.1 | 88–117 | 100% | 72–128 | **93%** |

The band at the next dose is **±14.5% as shown, ±28% as it should be**. The attainment probability at day 56
falls from 100% to 81%. The badge thresholds (`≥90%` green, `≥50%` amber — [ui.js:180](src/ui.js#L180)) are
applied to the optimistic quantity, so the app paints a confident green badge for a prediction that is one assay
standard deviation from failing.

**I checked the population-only case too, and it is fine.** With no samples the band is 95% of the true predictive
half-width — IIV dominates Σ for eculizumab, so the omission costs almost nothing. **This finding is specific to
the individualised fit, which is exactly the mode the app is for.**

*Fix.* Add a `predictive` variant alongside the current one rather than replacing it: propagate
`y = f(η)·(1 + ε_prop·z₁) + ε_add·z₂` through the same draws (one extra RNG per draw, negligible cost) and show
`P(measured > target)` as the headline, keeping the latent credible interval as the shaded band. One extra column
and one extra line in `findingsLines`. This is the single highest-value change in the report.

### A2 — Degenerate Monte-Carlo intervals in the printed report *(High)*

`batchMeansCI` clamps to `[0,1]` ([bayes.js:1672-1678](src/bayes.js#L1672)). When every draw is on one side of the
threshold the interval collapses to a point, and the report prints it as a 95% interval:

```
38.0 [34.9–41.3]     0% (0–0%)
87.6 [78.3–99.1]   100% (99–100%)
93.2 [82.8–107]    100% (100–100%)     ← printed, signed, and false
```

`ptaBadge` renders the tooltip *"Monte-Carlo 95% interval 100–100%"* on screen. A 95% interval of exactly
`[100,100]` claims the probability is known to infinite precision. It is not: the correct statement is
`> 99%` (rule of three on 2400 draws with 0 failures gives a one-sided 95% bound of 99.88%).

*Fix.* If `ci[0] === ci[1]`, render `> 99%` / `< 1%` and drop the interval. Never print a zero-width interval.

### A3 — The report quotes the most flattering of six ESS figures *(High)*

`precisionWord` correctly judges on `fit.essMin` ([ui.js:395](src/ui.js#L395)), but both the printed report
([ui.js:2677](src/ui.js#L2677)) and the on-screen "How this was calculated" line ([ui.js:1169](src/ui.js#L1169))
print `fit.essCL` — the clearance ESS only. For crovalimab, which estimates **six** random effects, this is
reporting the best of six and hiding the worst.

Ordinary crovalimab case (70 kg, 40 y, standard loading + q4w maintenance, 4 troughs):

```
eta       CL    V1    Q     V2    KA    F
ESS       263   238   241   216   236   106     ← F is the worst-informed, 2.5× the printed figure
R-hat    1.013 1.022 1.010 1.006 1.021 1.034
```

* What the printed report says: `MAP-Bayesian individualization + MCMC (2000 posterior draws, ESS ≈ 263, acceptance 0.30)`
* What the screen says: `intermediate (2000 posterior draws, ESS ≈ 263, acceptance 0.30)`

The word "intermediate" and the number "263" are talking past each other on the same line. And the parameter the
app itself flags as the trade-off risk in crovalimab's own assumptions — *"With sparse SC-only sampling,
absorption and clearance can partly trade off"* — is `F`, the one whose precision is not reported.

*Fix.* Print `ESS ≈ 263 (min 106, F)` — one extra token. Prefer `essMin` in the report line and show `essAll`
alongside `etaNames` in the diagnostics modal.

### A4 — The MC interval on P is invisible on screen *(Medium)*

`ptaBadge` puts the interval in a `title=` attribute. That is unreachable by touch, unreachable by keyboard, and
`null` for a screen reader. The printed report does show it inline ([ui.js:2758](src/ui.js#L2758)) — so the two
renderings of the same table carry different amounts of information. The chart's tooltip is the app's only other
numeric surface, and it is mouse-only (C4).

*Fix.* Render `P 99%` plus a small always-visible `±` superscript or a `details` per row; the existing
`ptaBadge` string-builder is already a pure function and trivially testable.

### A5 — Batch means across concatenated chains *(Medium, but currently benign)*

`postMat` rows are `draws` in chain order, so `batchMeansCI` cuts 12 batches through a 4-chain concatenation.
The estimator is only valid if batch boundaries respect chain structure.

**I tested this rather than assuming, and the width is correct here**: the app reports `P 73% (69–76%)`, and an
ESS-based calculation (ESS ≈ 600 of 2400 draws, `sqrt(.73·.27/600)·1.96 = 3.6` points) gives the same interval. So
this is not a live numerical error. But my first instinct — that the pooled interval was 2–3× too narrow — came
from comparing against per-chain CIs computed with smaller batches, and was **wrong**. Flagging only so the
assumption is written down and a future change to `keepEvery`/`maxKeep` does not quietly break it.

*Fix.* Comment the assumption at [bayes.js:1663](src/bayes.js#L1663), and compute batch means per chain and pool
the within-chain variances. Cheap, and removes a class of future bug.

### A6 / A7 — Smaller items *(Low)*

* [`ess()`](src/bayes.js#L434) is dead in production (`bulkEss` replaced it) but is still exported and tested. It
  contains a self-correcting hack — `tau` is computed twice, the second line subtracting a `rho_0` the first one
  double-counted, with the author's own commentary inline. It is the first thing a new reviewer will read and the
  least reliable code in the file. Delete it and its test, or fix the arithmetic.
* The MCMC adapts `logS` during the *kept* phase with a decaying `1/√adaptWin` gain
  ([bayes.js:583](src/bayes.js#L583)). This satisfies diminishing adaptation in spirit but the kept draws are not
  then from a time-homogeneous kernel, which is exactly what R-hat and batch means assume. The README is honest
  about it; the **printed report** is silent. One sentence in "Fit quality".

## 3. Pharmacometrics

### B1 — The half-life is a one-compartment number in a two-compartment model *(High)*

[`effHalfLife`](src/model.js#L451) is `ln2 · V1 / (CL + Vmax/(Km+C))`. That is the *one-compartment* elimination
half-life for the central compartment. All three models are two-compartment; the terminal slope is the slow
eigenvalue of `[[−(k₁₀+k₁₂), k₂₁], [k₁₂, −k₂₁]]`, which is nothing like `CL/V1`.

Computing the model's own terminal half-life from the app's own fitted parameters:

| Case | App displays | Model's terminal t½ | Ratio |
|------|-------------:|-------------------:|------:|
| Eculizumab, fitted patient (η_CL 0.41, η_V1 −0.14) | **5.5 d** | **19.3 d** | 3.5× |
| Ravulizumab, population typical | **29 d** | **45.9 d** | 1.6× |
| Crovalimab, population typical | **28.4 d** | **53.3 d** | 1.9× |

The eculizumab case is worst because the Michaelis-Menten term inflates `CL_eff` at trough concentrations, which
*shortens* the one-compartment number further while leaving the terminal slope alone.

This matters more than a cosmetic number error because **interval extension is the app's stated primary use
case** (`v0.13.0`: *"Routine TDM for these agents is largely about PROLONGING the dosing interval"*), and half-life
is precisely the quantity a clinician reaches for when reasoning about how long a new interval takes to settle.
The printed report repeats it as a headline: *"Half-life near the trough: ≈ 5.3 days."*

*Fix.* Report the terminal half-life from the matrix eigenvalues (5 lines), keep the one-compartment figure only
if labelled for what it is — a local slope estimate near the trough, not a half-life. Or drop it.

### B2 — `Eff. t½` is silently concentration-dependent *(Medium)*

It is evaluated at the *last* trough and changes as the patient's level changes, with no reference concentration
stated and no interval. The report's "How this was calculated" does say *"It shortens at higher concentrations
(saturable clearance)"*, which is honest; the on-screen value has neither. Add the reference concentration and
the 5–95% range (both are already computed per draw).

### B3 — Two numbers a pharmacometrician expects are absent *(Medium)*

* **No terminal half-life**, which is the first thing anyone checks against the literature.
* **Fitted Vmax/Km are never shown for eculizumab after individualisation** — only the population `VMAX`/`KM` in
  the no-sample branch. For a target-mediated drug, a single "Clearance CL (L/day)" is ambiguous: clearance is a
  function of concentration, and the app prints one number with an interval and no concentration attached.

### B4 — Residual error is printed as bare variances *(Medium)*

The report says: `Residual error model — additive 19.1 + proportional 0.0185`. Those are NONMEM **variances**,
with no units. A reader must remember that 0.0185 is a variance to recover a 13.6% CV, and that 19.1 is a
variance in (µg/mL)² to recover 4.4 µg/mL. Print `additive SD 4.4 µg/mL + proportional CV 13.6%` and keep the
variances in parentheses for anyone cross-checking the control stream.

### B5 / B6 — Latent risks, not live bugs *(Low)*

* `yMax = min(max·1.18, chartYMaxCap)` with `chartYMaxCap` 2400 (eculizumab). Past the cap, `Y()` clamps and the
  band renders as a **flat plateau** with no "axis clipped" indication. I could not trigger it: 4000 mg q7d at
  300 kg gives p95 max 1557 against a 2400 cap. Latent. If the cap is ever lowered or a drug is added, add an
  explicit "▲ clipped" marker.
* The explorer's "steady state" is `max(3, min(30, ceil(horizon/iv)))` cycles with `horizon` defaulting to 200 days
  ([bayes.js:1480](src/bayes.js#L1480)) — a function of an arbitrary constant, not of the drug's accumulation
  ratio. I checked all three drugs and it happens to be adequate (ravulizumab q8w reaches ~0.4% of steady state
  in 4 cycles), so this is right by luck rather than by construction. Replace with
  `n = ceil(ln(1e-4) / ln(1 − e^(−kel·iv)))`, which is exact and drug-agnostic.

## 4. UI and information design

### C1 — The chart is organised around the wrong number *(High)*

`yMax` is driven by `p95` **at the peak** ([ui.js:999-1008](src/ui.js#L999)). For the standard eculizumab patient
the axis runs 0–535, the target line sits at 75, and the entire decision-relevant band (88–117) occupies **about
15% of the plot height** — roughly 50 px on a desktop card and about 30 px at 390 px.

The chart is there to answer *"will the next trough clear 75?"* and it is currently scaled to answer *"how high
does the post-dose peak go?"* Nobody asks the second question, and the peak is already in the trough table's
neighbourhood by arithmetic rather than by inspection.

The log-axis toggle exists and is good, but it is off by default and never auto-suggested — and the app knows at
render time whether the band spans more than a decade.

*Fix.* Offer three y-scales and default sensibly: **"Trough"** (zoom to `[0, 1.4·max(trough p95, target)]`, peaks
run off the top with a clip marker), **"Full"** (current), **"Log"**. A `↕ Zoom to troughs` toggle beside the
existing log checkbox, defaulted on whenever `p95(trough)/p5(trough)` exceeds the current axis's useful resolution.

### C2 — The target label is drawn on top of the data *(High)*

`chart.js:228` writes the target label at `x = m.l + iw − 6`, `text-anchor: end`, `y = targetY − 5` with no
background and no halo. The target line by construction sits at the bottom of the interesting region, which is
exactly where the troughs and the observations are.

* Desktop: it runs through the `Today` vline and the projected-dose dotted line.
* 390 px: it sits across the concentration curve and two observation points.

*Fix.* Add a `paint-order="stroke"` white halo (`stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3" paint-order="stroke"`) — a
one-attribute fix — and/or place it just above the axis rather than just above the line.

### C3 — The phone legend is clipped; ~95% of the longest label is off-canvas *(High)*

v0.17.0 built a wrapping legend and sized the bottom margin to it. But `countLegendRows`
([chart.js:81](src/chart.js#L81)) caps each item's estimated width at the plot width for **row-packing purposes
only**:

```js
var wTxt = Math.min(iw, it.label.length * (fsLegend * 0.56) + 24);   // capped for counting…
```

…and the renderer at [chart.js:284](src/chart.js#L284) then writes the **full, uncapped** string with no wrap and
no truncation. Measured in the live phone layout (viewBox `0 0 340 383`):

```
"Projected dose (not entered, assumed q14d from the entered history)"   68 chars
× font-size 14 × 0.58                                            ≈ 552 units
right edge of viewBox                                            = 340 units
```

So ~210 units — about 60% of the string — render outside the SVG, and the item begins at `x = 72`, so roughly 95%
of the label is clipped. The screenshot confirms it: the legend reads
`Projected dose (not entered, assumed q14` and stops. The row-count reservation is correct and useless; the item
is simply longer than the card.

*Fix.* Shorten the label at the source (it is the only long one): `"Projected dose (not entered)"`, moving
"assumed q14d from the entered history" into the `title`. Then add `<title>` children to every legend `<text>` so
nothing is ever lost, and make `countLegendRows` use the same uncapped width the renderer does so a future long
label wraps instead of overflowing.

### C4 — The chart is unreadable on the layout it was redesigned for *(High)*

`chart.js` binds exactly two events: `mousemove` and `mouseleave`. There is no `touchstart`/`touchmove`, no
`pointermove`, and the hover rect has no `tabindex` (verified: `rectTabIndex: null`, `role="img"` on the SVG only).

On a touch device the tooltip is unreachable. Keyboard users cannot reach it either. The trough table is the
fallback — and it carries the median, the band, `P` and the date, but not the curve, not the peak, and not the
hover comparison against an observation.

This is a real gap precisely because v0.17.0 made the phone a first-class target and the phone is touch-only.

*Fix.* Bind `pointerdown`/`pointermove` (covers mouse, pen and touch in one path) on the hover rect; add
`tabindex="0"`, `role="application"` and arrow-key stepping; keep the tooltip mounted for screen readers via
`aria-live="polite"`.

### C9 — The v0.41.0 prior-treatment gate makes the common case unanswerable *(High)*

v0.41.0 added *"Was the patient treated with this drug before the first dose entered above?"* and hard-blocks the
forecast unless the answer is "No". Tested with a completely ordinary case — a patient on 900 mg q14d for a year,
with the last 8 doses and 4 troughs available, which is what most TDM consultations actually look like:

* Answer **"Yes, earlier doses are missing"** (the truthful answer) → Run stays disabled, with:
  *"Enter the earlier doses (then answer No), or use Steady state mode, to run the forecast."*
* Entering 26 more doses means 26 individual form submissions (there is no bulk entry — C11).
* Steady-state mode is offered but not explained here, and it is wrong for any patient whose regimen has changed.

The fix correctly eliminated a real failure mode (documented: CL 0.065 instead of 0.161, P 100% against a true
trough of 59). But a hard refusal replaced a silent wrong answer with a hard refusal, and the honest path is
now the one that does not work.

The right fix is not to weaken the gate but to give it a **third, safe answer**: *"Yes — treat the first entered
dose as already at steady state."* That is a well-posed problem: extend `windowStart` backwards by ~5 elimination
half-lives of pre-doses at the historical regimen, exactly as steady-state mode already does. It uses the same
machinery, it is the standard way this is handled in practice, and it makes the honest answer productive instead
of terminal.

### C5 — The caption under the chart contradicts the chart *(Medium)*

[index.html:246](index.html#L246) is static and always rendered:

> Individual = incorporates this patient's own measured levels · **Population = model only, no patient data yet** ·
> red points = measurements · dashed amber line = target · **faint dotted amber = a projected future dose**

Since v0.22.0 the population band is deliberately **not drawn** once an individual fit exists, and the projected-dose
marker only exists when a continuation was computed. Verified live with 4 measurements: the legend contains only
`Individual prediction 5–95%`, `Observation`, `Dose`, `Today`, `Projected dose` — and the caption still explains a
population band that is not on screen and still calls the user a novice for having no patient data.

*Fix.* Build the caption from the same `legend` array the chart is given, in [ui.js](src/ui.js) next to
`renderChart`, instead of hard-coding it in the HTML.

### C6 — Every trough timestamp is one minute wrong *(Medium)*

`troughTimesOf` returns `doses[i].t − 1e-6` days (−86.4 ms) so the simulation reads the concentration *before* the
dose. [ui.js:1204](src/ui.js#L1204) then formats that with `fmtDate`, which resolves to the minute:

```
Dose table:  30 Jun 2026, 09:00
Trough row:  30 Jun 2026, 08:59        ← every row, on screen and in the print report
```

This appears in the on-screen table, in the printed report's trough table, and in the findings line
*"Predicted trough before the next dose (06 Oct 2026, 08:59)"*. In a signed clinical document a timestamp that
disagrees with the dosing record by one minute reads as a data error, and it will be queried.

*Fix.* Format the trough from the *dose* time and label the column as the pre-dose draw, or round `t` to the
minute for display. The 1e-6 must stay in the engine; only the display should change.

### C7 — `µg/mL` is destroyed by `text-transform: uppercase` *(Medium)*

The results-table header renders as:

```
P(> 75 ΜG/ML)
```

`U+00B5 MICRO SIGN` uppercases to `U+039C GREEK CAPITAL LETTER MU`. Verified: `getComputedStyle(th).textTransform
=== "uppercase"`. The unit is no longer micrograms per millilitre in the app's single most important column
header.

*Fix.* `text-transform: none` on numeric/unit `th`s, or wrap the unit in a `<span class="unit">` with
`text-transform: none`.

### C8 — The Day column mixes number formats *(Medium)*

```
14.0    28.0    42.0    56.0    70.0    84.0    98.0    112
```

`fmtC` switches at 10 and 100, so a column of whole-number schedule days renders with a decimal until it crosses
100. `fmtDays` [ui.js:187](src/ui.js#L187) already exists and exists *precisely* for this ("*fmtC would render 14
as '14.0', which reads like a measured quantity rather than a schedule*") — it is just not used here.

*Fix.* `fmtDays(tr.t)` in the trough table and the report.

### C10 — No cancel, and the run is slow *(Medium)*

Measured on this machine via `node` (not the browser, so a real device is worse):

| Case | Wall time | Draws | min ESS |
|------|----------:|------:|--------:|
| Eculizumab (2-eta) | 4.9 s | 2400 | 558 |
| Crovalimab (6-eta) | 9.0 s | 2000 | **106** |
| Ravulizumab q8w, 1 y history | **13.6 s** | 2400 | 640 |

The Run button is disabled throughout, the main thread is blocked in MCMC chunks, and there is no abort control —
the only `cancel` element in the DOM is the report dialog's, which is hidden. The README claims "≈ 2–3 s"; a
ravulizumab patient with a year of history is 4–5× that before any browser overhead, on the phone layout the app
was explicitly built for.

*Fix.* A worker, or at minimum a `cancel` flag checked in the MCMC chunk loop (the loop already yields via `tick()`
every 200 iterations — this is a small change), and a live elapsed-time readout.

### C11–C14 — Smaller items *(Low)*

* **No bulk dose entry.** 26 historical doses = 26 submissions. Pairs badly with C9.
* **The explorer's candidate list is mostly dead space.** For the standard patient: q7d 339, **q14d 94.6 (P 100%)**,
  q21d 26.0, q28d 5.56, q35d 1.34, q42d 0.38, q56d 0.04, q70d 0.00. Six of eight are `P 0%` and below 10 µg/mL.
  The interval question has a binary answer for most patients and the app never notices; a dose scan is the more
  informative default in exactly these cases.
* **Chart hover says "Day 245"** ([chart.js:333](src/chart.js#L333)) while the table below gives a date. Pass the
  date through `cfg` and show both.
* **R-hat > 1.05 is warned about on screen but never reaches the print report.** The report is the artefact that
  leaves the building; convergence warnings belong in it.

---

## 5. What I checked and did **not** find

Listed so this work is not repeated. Several of these were my *first* hypotheses, and several were wrong.

1. **Ravulizumab CL–V1 covariance ignored in the prior.** I expected `priorOmega`'s `cov` to be dropped by
   `priorDraws` (which would silently diagonalise a published 2×2 `$OMEGA BLOCK`). It is not —
   [bayes.js:722](src/bayes.js#L722) applies it, and `omegaQuadVec` uses the exact 2×2 inverse. Sound.
2. **Batch-means CI too narrow.** I compared the app's `P 73% (69–76%)` against per-chain CIs computed with
   smaller batches and concluded it was 2–3× too narrow. **Wrong** — an ESS-based calculation reproduces the
   app's interval to within a point. The estimator is fine; only its chain-boundary assumption is undocumented (A5).
3. **The regimen explorer contradicts the forecast.** The explorer showed `q14d → 33.5 [30.4–37.9], P 0%` while the
   forecast showed `92.2, P 99%` for the same patient on the same regimen. This was **my own duplicated dose
   entry** (my setup script ran twice on one page), not an app bug — and the v0.41.0 duplicate-dose confirmation
   did exactly its job. On a clean run the explorer and forecast agree (94.6 vs 92.2, both P ≈ 100%), and I
   re-derived the steady state independently from the model: 91.9 µg/mL. **No bug.**
4. **Crovalimab chart continuation simulated as IV.** The prior review's Finding A does not reproduce;
   `contRoute` already reads `adminRoutes.subsequent`, and the whole block is gated off during loading. Fixed
   in v0.36.0.
5. **y-axis band clipping.** Could not trigger even at 4000 mg q7d / 300 kg (p95 max 1557 vs a 2400 cap).
6. **Likelihood.** Exact Gaussian with the `log(σ²)` term that is genuinely η-dependent under proportional error;
   M3 censoring `−2·logΦ((LLOQ−pred)/σ)`; the variance floor is a MAP guard, not a claimed data term. All correct.
7. **Convergence plumbing.** `splitRhat` and `bulkEss` share `splitChainStats`. `converged = iter < maxIter`, so a
   budget-exhausted simplex cannot masquerade as a mode. The Laplace fallback to `0.25·diag(Ω)` is flagged via
   `covFallback` and reaches `precisionWord`. The `1e5`-day unit guard and the infusion-duration backstop are both
   real and correctly placed.
8. **Vmax/Km, allometry, the `WT_REF` 75 kg crovalimab reference, the SC depot compartment and the logit-transformed
   F** are all transcribed consistently between `model.js` and the control streams as far as I traced them.

---

## 6. Suggested order of work

1. **A1** — add the predictive (Σ-inclusive) probability and band. Highest clinical value, self-contained, one RNG
   per draw.
2. **B1** — replace `effHalfLife` with the terminal half-life, or relabel it honestly. Five lines.
3. **A2 + A3** — degenerate-interval rendering and `essMin` in the report. Two small edits, both in printed output.
4. **C2 + C6 + C7 + C8** — four one-line rendering fixes, all of which currently put wrong-looking text into a
   signed clinical document.
5. **C3 + C4** — legend truncation and pointer/keyboard support. Together they make the phone layout usable.
6. **C9** — add the "treat the first entered dose as at steady state" third answer.
7. **C1** — trough-zoom y-axis, with a default that depends on the band/target ratio.
8. **C5, C10, B3, B4, C14** — the remaining Medium/Low items.

Per this repo's own rule, each of these should be pinned by a new `tests/test_v042.js` and **shown red against the
current code before it is shown green** — and the A1/A2/A3/C6/C7 class of bug is exactly the kind that a
source-text assertion cannot catch, so those want a rendered-output assertion against `reportHtml`, which is
already a pure function and already has a test suite.
